status: Rules in effect; SB 947 and SB 951 signed
law: Civil Rights Council rules ; SB 947 (Ch. 859); SB 951 (Ch. 860)
what_it_requires: State anti-discrimination rules spell out that using an automated decision system that discriminates is illegal, just like any other hiring practice. The rules also cover record keeping. SB 947 adds limits on using AI to discipline or fire workers (see below). SB 951 adds AI details to mass-layoff notices.
who_it_covers: Employers with 5 or more workers (covered by California's Fair Employment and Housing Act); SB 947 reaches employers of every size; SB 951 covers employers already under Cal/WARN
starts: Rules in effect Oct 1, 2025; SB 947 starts July 1, 2027; SB 951 starts Jan 1, 2027

law: SB26-189 (replaces the 2024 Colorado AI Act, SB24-205)
what_it_requires: If you use an automated tool that heavily shapes a big decision about a person, including a job decision, you must tell them first. If the result goes against them, you must explain it in plain language within 30 days and, where reasonable, let them fix wrong data and ask for a human review. Keep records for 3 years.
who_it_covers: Businesses using these tools with Colorado residents. We found no small-business exemption in the text.

law: HB 3773 (Public Act 103-0804) HB 2557, AI Video Interview Act (Public Act 101-0260); HB 53 (Public Act 102-0047)
what_it_requires: Makes it a civil rights violation to use AI in a way that discriminates in hiring, firing, promotion, discipline or other job decisions, or to use zip codes as a stand-in for a protected group. Employers must tell workers when they use AI for these decisions. If AI scores recorded video interviews, you must tell the applicant in writing, explain how it works and get their consent. Limits sharing the videos and requires deleting them on request. Employers that rely only on AI to pick who gets an in-person interview must report applicant demographics to the state.
who_it_covers: Employers covered by the Illinois Human Rights Act, which includes very small employers Employers hiring for jobs based in Illinois that use AI to review video interviews

what_it_requires: You can't use facial recognition during a job interview unless the applicant signs a consent waiver.

status: City law; state laws cover government only
law: NYC Local Law 144 (city law); state S 822 (2025) and S 8831 (2026)
what_it_requires: In New York City, employers using an automated hiring or promotion tool must get a yearly bias audit, post the results and notify candidates. The two state laws only cover state and local government agencies.
who_it_covers: Employers and staffing agencies hiring for jobs in New York City

law: HB 149, Texas Responsible AI Governance Act
what_it_requires: You can't build or use AI with the intent to unlawfully discriminate against a protected group. A tool that has an unequal effect is not enough on its own to break this law.
who_it_covers: Anyone doing business in Texas. Only the Attorney General can enforce it, and you get 60 days to fix a problem first.
